title: A document may declare several named timelines

v:
One diagram often has more than one story to tell — a checkout that pays by card and one that pays
by wallet walk the same class diagram in different orders. Until now a document declared its
`timeline:` block at most once, so an author who wanted two paths copied the whole diagram into a
second `.srn` file and kept the two structures in sync by hand. We let one document declare
**several named timeline blocks** over one structure, and let the caller choose which one applies.
Board plan: `.scratch/multi-timeline/spec.md`.

## The rules

- A named block opens with `timeline <name>:`, where the name is `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+` and
  case-sensitive. It runs to the next timeline header or the end of the document; nothing else
  closes it. Blank lines still take no step number (ADR-0012).
- The unnamed `timeline:` stays, as the shorthand for a document with exactly one timeline. A
  document whose only block is `timeline:` parses, validates, renders and animates exactly as
  before.
- Each of these is an error-severity diagnostic and costs the whole document, like any other
  timeline grammar error: mixing the unnamed header with named ones; two unnamed headers (this
  replaces the old `Unrecognized timeline action: "timeline:"`); a repeated name (reported on the
  later header); a malformed name.
- Every block is resolved on its own: its steps count from 1, anything *it* never mentions is
  visible from its step 0, and enter/exit dedupe and the connector warning look only inside it.
- Every block is validated on every render, whichever one is applied, so choosing a timeline never
  makes a problem appear or vanish — the same promise `timeline: false` already keeps. A
  diagnostic that resolution raises inside a named block starts `timeline <name>:` rather than
  `timeline:`; an unnamed document's messages are unchanged.
- `render()`'s `timeline` option widens to `boolean | string`: `true` or omitted applies the first
  block, `false` draws the full diagram, a string applies the block of that name. The result lists
  the named blocks as `timelines`, in document order (`[]` when the document has none, or only the
  unnamed one). A name the document does not declare throws a `RangeError`: it is the caller's
  mistake, not the author's, and no edit to the document could fix it, so it is not a diagnostic.

## Considered Options

- **Build it in board, not core** — board splits the text into one document per path and renders
  each. Rejected. Board does not parse (ADR-0005); doing so here would be a second timeline
  grammar outside the one `parseTimelineBlock` exists to own, would shift every diagnostic's line
  number, and would split `.srn` into a dialect only board reads — a multi-timeline file would fail
  outright in every other viewer instead of degrading to its first path.
- **A timeline never mentioning an element hides it** — closer to the intuition of a "path", but
  it would make the same block mean different things depending on whether it is named, and would
  break the rule that a named block behaves exactly as if it were the document's only one.
  Rejected; each block keeps the existing step-0 rule. A verb that hides at step 0 is a separate
  decision for when someone needs it.
- **Switch timelines without re-rendering** (`result.useTimeline(name)` returning a fresh
  controller over the same SVG) — deferred. Re-rendering with a name is the pattern board already
  uses for the full diagram; a second way to switch can be added later without changing this one.
- **Shared-prefix syntax** for paths that begin alike, and **display labels** separate from names
  — deferred; nothing here closes either off.

## Consequences

Amends ADR-0002 (`01M4GA39JT3NG7R0YCZK0XKM6T`), whose block was implicitly one per document, and
ADR-0012 (`01M4GA3DR0XA2JJXZ94MHDH8PQ`), under which a second `timeline:` line was an unrecognized
action. A viewer that never passes a name still works and shows the first path; offering the rest
is the viewer's choice, which is why `RenderOptions.timeline` documents it.

## Amendment (the board's controls in the full diagram)

Choosing a timeline is a capability of the API and a control of the built-in bar, and the two
answer the full diagram differently. `board.setTimeline(name)` called from code while the full
diagram shows still leaves it and applies that timeline: a host that offers its own switcher keeps
the power to do so. The built-in control bar's Timeline dropdown, however, is **disabled** while the
full diagram shows, like Prev, Play, Next, Reset and Play interval. The first build left it as the
one control still usable there, picking from it leaving the full diagram; in the browser that read
as an inconsistency rather than a shortcut — every other step control says "nothing to do here",
and the one that remained looked like an oversight. Leaving the full diagram stays the Full diagram
button's job. Board plan: `.scratch/multi-timeline/T06-timeline-dropdown-disabled-in-full-diagram.md`.
